According to an ordinal regression model (proportional-odds, logit link), controlling for BCG vaccination status and patient interaction variables (work hours, patients seen, expected patient interaction), each additional ongoing medical condition (MHONGO) is associated with approximately a 26% increase in the odds of higher COVID-19 severity (OR = 1.26, 95% CI 0.93–1.71; coefficient 0.2311, p = 0.136).

Details: analysis set n = 151 subjects with a COVID-19 adverse event and non-missing severity (severity = subject-level max AESEV, categories 1–4: 54/79/11/7). n_ongoing = deduplicated (case-normalized) count of MHONGO='Yes' records per subject. Model: severity ~ BCG + work_hours + patients_seen + expect_interact + n_ongoing (statsmodels OrderedModel). Coefficients: n_ongoing 0.2311 (SE 0.1549); BCG 0.1251 (p=0.70); expect_interact −0.1958 (p=0.57); work_hours/patients_seen levels all p>0.1. Odds increase = (exp(0.2311)−1)×100% = 26.0% (95% CI −7.0% to 70.7%). Brant test for the proportional-odds assumption: chi2=61.1, df=14, p<0.001 (driven mainly by quasi-separation of the 2-subject work_hours>80 level); n_ongoing showed the smallest cross-threshold coefficient variation (range 0.54), and the estimate was stable across specifications (24.0–24.8% in sensitivity models). Limitations: small sample (n=151; only 18 subjects in the two highest severity categories), so the effect is positive but not statistically significant at 0.05.
